ops.title: Body operations
ops.normNowRef: Reference flux for cd/klm is {{v}} lm ({{kind}}) — it becomes 1000 lm, candela values become equal to cd/klm.
ops.normFactorNote: Intensities and flux are multiplied by the factor.
ops.normNote: Intensities and lamp flux are scaled together: the distribution shape and cd/klm values stay the same, so does the LOR.
ops.axisNote_z: Z is the vertical axis: C0 moves to C+angle (right-hand rule, counter-clockwise seen from above).
ops.axisNote_x: X runs along C0: a positive angle tilts the nadir towards C90.
ops.axisNote_y: Y runs along C90: a positive angle tilts the nadir towards C180.
ops.rotateSteps: Each rotation is a separate step in the history; the order matters.
ops.symNote: Intensities are averaged over mirrored planes; flux is preserved.
ops.regridNote: Values at new nodes are interpolated. The C step must divide the stored range (90°, 180° or 360°).
ops.sumNote: Intensities are summed in the far field; rotations are applied in order X → Y → Z; offsets enlarge the luminous dimensions. The result opens as a new file.
ops.historyNote: Click a step to go back to it. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y — undo and redo.

err.zero-flux: Flux is zero — nothing to normalise
err.g-step: γ step {{step}}° does not divide the {{span}}° range

ops.preview3dNote: Both bodies share one scale (radius = the larger of the two peaks) and rotate together.
ops.smoothNote: Gaussian smoothing on the sphere: each value becomes an average of neighbouring directions weighted by angular distance. The width is the kernel FWHM: details narrower than it (noise, measurement ripple) are smoothed out, a narrow beam peak drops slightly. Grid and symmetry stay the same.
ops.smoothNarrow: The width does not exceed the grid step (C {{c}}°, γ {{g}}°) — neighbouring nodes barely contribute, there will be no effect. Refine the grid first or increase the width.

batch.title: Batch processing
batch.dropHere: Drop IES / LDT files or folders here
batch.dropHint: or click to choose files. Subfolders are read too.
batch.dropOverlay: Release to add the files to the batch
batch.takeOpenModified: Modified files are taken in their current state (with operations)
batch.recipeOff: No operations: files are taken as they are (e.g. for conversion, charts and the summary table).
batch.recipeFromHistoryDone: {{n}} steps taken from the history of "{{file}}"
batch.recipeEmpty: No steps. Add operations below — they are applied to every file in order.
batch.variantsOff: No variants: one output per source file.
batch.variantsNote: For every file — one file per row: same distribution shape, intensities scaled by the flux ratio, CCT, CRI, power and lamp taken from the row. Empty cell — value of the source file.
batch.varPastePlaceholder: Paste rows from Excel (Ctrl+V). The first row may be a header: Suffix, CCT, Flux, Factor, CRI, Power, Lamp.
batch.varPasteNothing: No table rows in the clipboard
batch.varNote: Ctrl+V in the table adds rows from Excel. Flux with % is a factor.
batch.namingNote: Duplicate names get _2, _3. The archive name is asked when saving.
batch.cmykNote: CMYK — in PDF and EPS; SVG is always RGB
batch.chartsFolders: Polar and linear charts go to the polar/ and linear/ folders.
batch.chartsUse: Layout and settings as on the chart tabs: {{layout}}, {{unit}}, font {{font}}, style "{{style}}", labels {{lang}}.
batch.commonScaleFixed: A scale maximum of {{v}} is set on the chart tab — it is used for all files.
batch.summaryNote: Flux, power, efficacy, Imax, beam and field angles, LOR, CCT, CRI and check issues per file. XLSX has an "Issues" sheet, CSV a separate file. IES/LDT pairs with the same name are compared.
batch.needVariants: The variant table has no rows with a suffix
batch.done: Done: read {{read}} of {{inputs}}, {{outputs}} sets, {{entries}} files in the archive
batch.issuesFound: Check issues: {{e}} errors, {{w}} warnings — see the summary table.
batch.errors: Not processed: {{n}} (details in the log inside the archive)
batch.varAngleNote: Lamps {{list}} have a beam angle. Scaling keeps the same distribution: if the angle differs from the lamp in the source measurement, a separate measurement is needed — such variants are flagged in the summary table.
